text: Hello and welcome to our live text coverage of the Premier League clash between Brighton and Hove Albion and Tottenham at the Amex Stadium.

Brighton have won just two of their past 12 top-flight matches - albeit they have advanced to the Europa League knockout rounds during that period - with their most recent result a 1-1 draw at Crystal Palace last Thursday.
Despite their lack of victories, Roberto De Zerbi's side are ninth in the Premier League heading into this contest.

After a drop in form that saw them take one point from a possible 15, Tottenham have since returned to their early season form thanks to successive wins over Newcastle United, Nottingham Forest and Everton.

A fourth successive victory today would live them back above Manchester City into fourth place, having played a game more, while a victory by three goals would lift them above third-placed Aston Villa on goal difference.
Brighton subs: Bart Verbruggen, Mahmoud Dahoud, Adam Lallana, Jakub Moder, Carlos Baleba, Evan Ferguson, Pervis Estupinan, Benicio Baker-Boaitey, Luca Barrington.
Tottenham subs: Bryan Gil, Eric Dier, Giovani Lo Celso, Fraser Forster, Ashley Phillips, Alejo Veliz, Yago Santiago, Jamie Donley, Alfie Dorrington.
Brighton will be well rested on the back of their draw with Crystal Palace seven days ago - a real rarity at this time of the season - yet De Zerbi has still made four changes from that contest.
Steele returns in goal in place of Verbruggen, while Welbeck replaces Baleba as a reward for his goal against Palace.
Buonanotte and Milner are also recalled to the XI, with Simon Adingra and Kaoru Mitoma missing out on the squad.
Tottenham have made two changes from their win over Everton.
Udogie is back involved and takes over from the injured Cristian Romero, which should see Emerson play alongside Ben Davies - another natural full-back - in the heart of defence.
Hojbjerg is also named in the starting line-up in place of Oliver Skipp, who misses out on the squad entirely today due to injury.
Brighton have lost their last two Premier League home games against Tottenham without scoring.
The hosts have hardly had the best time of things over the past couple of months, but they will target this match as a chance to properly kick-start their league campaign.
Kick-off is now just moments away.
Tottenham get us up and running at the Amex Stadium in this Premier League contest! These two sides have provided great entertainment this season, so let us hope for more of the same today.
As you would expect, Tottenham are looking to pass it out from the back even when under pressure from Brighton's high press.
Spurs work the ball into the box and it is cleared away.
These opening few minutes have set the tone nicely.
Tottenham are looking the livelier, but Son is caught offside as this latest attack comes to nothing.
Johnson wins his side a free-kick within shooting distance after being caught by Igor.
Porro is the player stood over the ball...
Porro blasts the free-kick straight into the wall.
Brighton, who have barely had a touch of the ball, can breathe again.
Richarlison sprays the ball out to Johnson on the right.
The Welshman plays a quick one-two and looks to pass the ball into the box, but it is overhit.
This has been a very positive start from the visitors.
SAVE! The first save of the match is made by Vicario, completely against the run of play.
Porro is disposed and the Brighton counter ends with Welbeck aiming to bend one into the far corner, but he does not get enough whip on it and Vicario keeps it out.

events.action: bend one into the far corner

text: INCREDIBLE STOP!! Well that Vicario save a minute or so ago was decent, but this was out of the top drawer.
A blocked shot lands in the path of Welbeck, who steadies himself and picks his spot about eight yards out.
Vicario gets back to his feet and somehow pushes the ball to safety.
Welbeck cannot believe it!
Spurs dominated the first five minutes or so, barely giving their opponents a touch, but since then Brighton have twice tested Vicario.
That second save to keep out Welbeck really was superb.
Tottenham have been a little more controlled with their possession over the past few minutes.
The Vicario double save appears to have made them reassess their gung-ho approach.
GOOOAAALLL!!! BRIGHTON 1-0 TOTTENHAM! Joao Pedro drives into the box, then back out of it, before picking out Hinshelwood.
The unmarked youngster takes a touch to settle himself and then absolutely thumps a shot past Vicario to give Brighton the lead.
This was very good play from Joao Pedro.
He got at the Tottenham defence, who were scared to put a foot in, and then found a team-mate to emphatically fire home.
That is Hinshelwood's second Premier League goal.
He may only be aged 18, and he is playing at full-back today, but he took that like a 20-goal-a-season striker.
Spurs are far too open.
Tottenham have not really changed their approach since falling behind, and nor would you expect them to on the basis of what we have seen of Ange Postecoglou's time in charge.
This is a bit of a difference for them as they so often take the lead in matches.
ANOTHER SAVE! Vicario is keeping Tottenham in this match.
The Italian is equal to Joao Pedro's shot and gets away with it as the fumbled save is cleared.
Terrible defending from Spurs there, it must be said.
Vicario was not happy with Porro and Emerson for failing to get across to Joao Pedro and cut out the shot.
Welbeck and Joao Pedro are having plenty of joy so far at the Amex Stadium.
Joao Pedro again tries to get at Tottenham, but all he has to show for this latest attack is a corner.
PENALTY APPEAL! A corner is sent in by Gross and Van Hecke heads it against the post.
However, Kulusevski clearly drags back on Welbeck's shirt inside the box and the referee, after play resumed for a minute or so, is being asked to check the pitchside monitor.
PENALTY TO BRIGHTON! Kulusevski clearly pulled back on the shirt of Welbeck, who was looking to get to the ball after Van Hecke's header had come back off the frame of the goal.
There can be no complaints from Tottenham's perspective after VAR intervened.
Kulusevski is booked for preventing Welbeck from getting on the end of the ball in front of goal.
GOOOAAAALLL!! BRIGHTON LEAD 2-0! Joao Pedro has been very lively so far today and he has a goal to go with his assist.
He sends the penalty into the bottom-left corner, the opposite way to Vicario's dive, and Brighton have some breathing space.
That really was poor from Kulusevski.
He held on to Welbeck's shirt for an age and VAR was always going to intervene.
It is already a long way back for Spurs.
This is the first time Tottenham have trailed by two goals in a Premier League game under Postecoglou.
The visitors looked lively early on, but they have yet to muster a shot on target.
Brighton just need to keep doing what they are doing.
Son's shot is sarcastically cheered by the home fans as it trickles behind, but it took a deflection so a corner is awarded.
Porro takes and Igor easily heads it clear.
The attack remains alive and Johnson's superb cross is just out of Richarlison's reach.
Welbeck wins a corner off Davies, but this latest set-piece comes to nothing.
Dunk tries to wrestle back the ball but it goes behind for a goal-kick.
OFF THE POST! What a strike this is from Milner! He skips inside and sends a curling shot from the edge of the box rattling against the right-hand post.
Vicario was nowhere near it.
BIG CHANCE FOR SPURS! Porro sends a great ball over the top right into the path of Johnson.
The Wales international halts his run, though, and the momentum completely goes as he sends a shot into Igor.
On what is his 50th Premier League appearance, this is the first time that Joao Pedro has scored and assisted in a match in the competition.
Porro has had a torrid time of things defensively so far on the Tottenham right.
Kulusevski is not able to bring a ball under control, which is becoming a theme for Tottenham.
Still, the visitors are starting to look more threatening all of a sudden as we fast approach half-time on England's South Coast.
GOAL DISALLOWED! Buonanotte thinks he has given Brighton a third goal, but he is just offside when meeting - and converting - Welbeck's cross.
That was a delightful pass and a delightful finish on the half-volley, but the officials made the right call.
Richarlison spins in the box and decides against shooting, instead teeing up Son, but the South Korea international is crowded out.
He perhaps could have let it run to Johnson behind him.
What should have been a simple pass into the path of Son is horribly overhit, summing things up from Tottenham's perspective.
Joao Pedro thinks he is in behind again up the other end, but the offside flag denies him.
Buonanotte is the first player to be cautioned as he takes too long to retreat when Spurs attempt to take a quick free-kick.
VICARIO BAILS OUT TOTTENHAM! Porro plays the ball straight into the path of Joao Pedro, who is clean through on goal.
The Brighton attacker tries to dink the ball over Vicario, but he gets his hand to it and the hosts only have a corner and not a goal.
OFF THE POST! Out of absolutely nowhere, a quick counter culminates in Johnson playing a pass to Richarlison that is crying out for a first-time hit.
Richarlison does just that from the edge of the box and clips the outside of the post, with the help of a slight deflection off Dunk's studs.
Five minutes have been added on at the end of this hugely eventful first half at the Amex Stadium.
There has been plenty of action at both ends.
Son bends a shot agonisingly wide of the post from 19 yards after being picked out by Udogie.
Brighton will be happy to hear the half-time whistle.
HALF-TIME: BRIGHTON AND HOVE ALBION 2-0 TOTTENHAM
Brighton take a 2-0 lead into half-time against Tottenham.
Joao Pedro teed up Hinshelwood for Brighton's 11th-minute opener and then scored the second himself from the penalty spot after Kulusevski had pulled back on the shirt of Welbeck.
Richarlison clipped the outside of the post for Spurs towards the end of the half, but Brighton themselves hit the post through Milner and had a Buonanotte goal disallowed for offside.
Vicario also made four saves, the best of which saw him deny Joao Pedro from a one-on-one.
Spurs have so often led in Premier League games under Ange Postecoglou, but they find themselves two goals down in a match for the first time since he took charge.
Brighton are good value for their lead, but Tottenham showed in the final 10 minutes of the half that they can easily find a route back into this contest.
It goes without saying that the third goal in this match - should there be one - will be vital.
Estupinan, returning from an injury lay-off, is on for Igor in the only half-time substitution.
Brighton, leading thanks to Hinshelwood's strike and Joao Pedro's penalty, get us back under way at the Amex Stadium.

OFFSIDE! Richarlison thinks he has given Tottenham a route back into the game within 40 seconds of the restart, but his well-taken strike past Steele is rightly ruled out for offside as soon as the ball hits the net.
A free-kick is sent deep into the Tottenham box and hooked back centrally by Milner.
It is helped behind for a corner, which Milner - after a delay due to some pulling in the box - swings in for Vicario to get to, albeit at the expense of another set-piece.
A third corner in a row for Brighton is cleared by Porro at the front post.
Richarlison scored an offside goal for Spurs near enough right from kick-off, but since then there has been no danger for the hosts.
Son is on the ball inside the box - always a good thing if you are a Tottenham fan - but two Brighton players are quickly on top of him.
Spurs are having very little joy at the moment.
The second half has not been quite as all-action as the first so far, which you would imagine is a good thing for Brighton.
The onus is on Tottenham to find the next goal in this contest.
SO CLOSE! Richarlison controls Son's pass inside the box, turns and sends a shot curling wide of the post.
That all came about as a result of Tottenham's high press catching Brighton cold.
Sloppy play for Brighton for the second time in as many minutes.
Johnson plays in Richarlison, whose first-time shot is too close to Steele.
It would not have counted anyway as the offside flag is up.
ANOTHER SAVE! Tottenham have well and truly ramped up the pressure.
Udogie's first shot is blocked and then his second one is saved by Steele.
Son then claims a penalty for a shove in the box - or possibly just outside - but the referee is having none of it.
Richarlison pushes Joao Pedro in the throat and earns himself a yellow card.
Brighton have a penalty appeal for a possible handball against Richarlison.
However, the Brazil international is on his way to ground from a header and has no idea where the ball is.
VAR tells the referee to play on.
One 19-year-old is replaced by another as Baleba comes on for Buonanotte.
We have played just over 15 minutes of the second half and it is as you were from the end of the first half.
Tottenham have had their moments, but they have not really warranted a goal.
DISALLOWED! Richarlison meets Kulusevski's pass in behind and slots the ball past Steele, but once again the offside flag denies him.
The officials were quick to make the call and replays show they were correct - no need for VAR to intervene.
GOOOOAAALLL!!! WHAT A STRIKE! This is superb from the returning Estupinan.

He puts his foot through the ball from a good 25-30 yards out and the ball does all sorts in the air - it swerves, it dips, it goes this way and that - and ultimately ends with Vicario failing to get anything to it.
Milner will be rather embarrassed to be credited with this assist from a short corner.
This goal was all about Estupinan's strike.
That is a goal of the season contender, easily.
Since the start of the 2017-18 season, Richarlison has been booked more times (36) than any other forward in the Premier League.
The Brazil international has not had a great game today, having also missed some good chances.
Richarlison makes way for Tottenham after a disappointing game.
Lo Celso comes on, which may mean Son moving centrally.
It is a double change for the visitors as Sarr is replaced by Gil.
Since the start of November, only Nottingham Forest (19) have conceded more goals in the Premier League than Spurs (18).
That is a pretty damning statistic, and one that suggests Postecoglou's tactics do need looking at.
Ferguson is brought on in place of Welbeck, who has put in a solid shift today without really having anything to show for it from a personal perspective.
Milner has been very good today.
The experienced midfielder is replaced by Moder for the final 20 minutes or so.
Johnson has had his moments today, but it just has not been Tottenham's - or his - day.
Veliz is given a run-out at the Amex Stadium in his place.
Hojbjerg blasts the ball at Moder's shin, but it is the Brighton player who is showed the yellow card for delaying the restart.
Tottenham are still plugging away to their credit, but you do have to fear a fourth goal could easily be conceded.
This has been a superb display from Brighton, who are now well and truly back on track in the Premier League.
ANOTHER BRIGHTON PENALTY! Lo Celso takes a bit of fellow substitute Ferguson in the process of getting the ball and the referee points to the penalty spot.
Talk about making an instant impact from the Brighton striker's point of view!
PENALTY STANDS AFTER VAR CHECK! After a bit of a delay, Brighton will finally get the chance to take the penalty.
VAR checked for a possible Brighton offside in the build-up to Lo Celso's challenge on Ferguson, but there was no infringement.
GOOOAAAALLL!!!! BRIGHTON 4-0 TOTTENHAM!! This is getting embarrassing for Tottenham now.
Joao Pedro this time goes to his right, and Vicario this time goes to his left, which results in the same outcome - a second successfully converted penalty for the hosts.
Ferguson is so nearly through on goal, but Udogie does well to get his body in between the Brighton player and the ball.
It is damage limitation time for Tottenham at this point.
A number of Tottenham supporters are beginning the journey back to London already as the away end clears.
Brighton have looked so much better today, which could partly be down to having a full week's rest, or perhaps simply because De Zerbi's tactics have been spot on.
GOOOAAALLL!!! TOTTENHAM HAVE ONE BACK! Kulusevski refuses to give up and blocks a pass from Dunk.
It falls to Son, who finds Veliz alongside him to convert past Steele.
That is a first goal in Tottenham colours for Veliz to make it 4-1.
Son took a quick glance up and saw Veliz, who grabs a consolation goal for Spurs.
Dunk is cautioned for his follow-through challenge on Kulusevski in the direct build-up to Veliz's goal.
He will now miss Brighton's next game, which is at West Ham.
Play is delayed getting back under way as Kulusevski requires treatment as a result of that challenge from Dunk on him.
On another day, the Brighton player could have been shown a red card.
Perhaps the fact Veliz scored helped him in a way.
Udogie tries to zip a cross across the six-yard box, but the ball is cut out for a corner.
This is a strong finish from Spurs, but it is surely too little too late.
GOOOAAALL!! NOW THEN! Gil plays the ball to Porro, who swings a cross towards the back post for Davies to get above Dunk and head past Steele.
That is a great header - albeit one Brighton should have done better to cut out - and Tottenham are incredibly back in this game as it is now 4-2.
Porro's delivery into the six-yard box was spot on, but full credit to Davies for getting on the end of it and finding the net.
That is his first league goal in over a year.

Joao Pedro has scored all eight of the penalties he has taken for Brighton this season, while he hs netted more from the spot than any other player across Europe's big five leagues in all competitions in 2023-24.
For the first time today, Brighton's players are looking a little anxious.
Son throws himself to the ground and wants a penalty, but there is not sufficient contact from Estupinan.
Tottenham are really starting to turn the screw now.
A third goal would make things seriously interesting.
Nine minutes have been added on so there is still plenty of time!
Gil's appeal for a possible handball inside the box is also turned down.
You cannot blame the Spurs players for doing everything to try to win their side a penalty.
After a couple of scary moments for Brighton, Kulusevski's drive fails to test Steele and the hosts can finally breathe.
Three of the nine added-on minutes have been played.
Who on earth saw a scenario in which Brighton were rather holding on at this stage of the match at 4-0 up?!
Joao Pedro leaves the field to be replaced by Lallana.

Lo Celso says something to the departing player on his way off the field - possibly a complaint at how long he was taking to head for the sidelines - and the Brighton man reacts by urging the crowd to make more noise.
OFF THE POST!! Hojbjerg's sweetly hit shot, after being picked out by makeshift striker Udogie, comes clean back off the post.
Porro's follow-up shot hits Estupinan in the chest, but that does not stop the Spurs players claiming a penalty for handball.
Tottenham really have given it their all in the last 15 minutes or so, but they ultimately left themselves with too much to do.
There are positives to take out of this match, but more negatives.
The visitors have not really been able to build any attacks in the past couple of minutes.
The Hojbjerg shot that struck the post will likely be the final meaningful act of this thrilling game.
Son gets across his man but cannot make the contact he would have liked on the ball as he finds the side-netting.
That should be that.
The referee plays advantage and that almost pays off as Gil drives forward and powers a shot over the bar from outside the box.
FULL-TIME: BRIGHTON AND HOVE ALBION 4-2 TOTTENHAM
Brighton beat Tottenham 4-2 to snap their opponents' three-game winning run and climb up to eighth in the Premier League, six points behind Tottenham who stay in fifth.
Joao Pedro set up Hinshelwood to open the scoring in a thrilling game and scored the second himself from the penalty spot.
Half-time substitute Estupinan scored a goal of the season contender to put Brighton three up just after the hour, and a fourth arrived via another Joao Pedro penalty.

Both goalkeepers were called into the action, while the posts were rattled multiple times, but Tottenham's comeback fell short as they could not add to goals from Veliz and Davies in the final 10 minutes.
Tottenham will look to respond to this defeat when they host Bournemouth on Sunday, while Brighton head to West Ham on Tuesday for their next match.
That is all for today's live text coverage, thanks for joining!
